description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and the accuracy (ACC, %) (y-axis) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” spans from 0 to 10⁴ on a logarithmic scale, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 60% to 80% on a linear scale, with major gridlines and tick labels at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The “Base” method (black line with circle markers) starts at approximately 61% at co-occurrence 1 and gradually increases to about 66.5% at 10⁴. The “FT” method (blue line with downward triangle markers) begins at ~62.5% and rises to ~67%. The “IKE” method (red line with upward triangle markers) starts at ~64.5% and reaches ~68.5%. The “MEND” method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at ~65.5% and climbs to ~74.5%. The “MEMIT” method (purple line with circle markers) starts at ~65.5% and increases to ~73%. The “ROME” method (green line with square markers) begins at ~73% and plateaus near 77.5% after 10², showing the highest performance across most of the range. All lines exhibit a generally increasing trend with diminishing returns as co-occurrence number grows, except ROME, which stabilizes early.
